page: Microsoft Azure D64d_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDv5 server family. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz, this instance provides 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It features 256 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The server runs on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and utilizes the x86_64 architecture. It includes 2458 GB of local SSD storage, offering high-capacity, low-latency local disk space directly attached to the instance.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong multi-core capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core CPU, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU scores placing in the top 25% tier. Large-block uncached memory read and write bandwidths also perform in the top 25%, reaching 291.88 GB/sec and 134.9 GB/sec respectively. Single-core performance, such as Geekbench single-core and stress-ng single-core, falls within the average middle 50% range. The instance demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, software compilation, and static web serving throughput, while LLM inference speeds for small to large models remain in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D64d_v5 offers a highly dense resource allocation, balancing compute, memory, and high-capacity local SSD storage. This configuration is suitable for workloads requiring fast local scratch space and robust multi-threaded processing without the added cost of dedicated memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. Appropriate workloads include relational databases, multi-threaded software compilation, high-throughput web serving, and enterprise-grade general-purpose applications.
